biography: Carlos Eduardo 'Cacá' Bueno, born in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, practically breathed motorsport from birth. His father, a recreational kart racer, had Cacá strapped into a kart almost before he could walk. While other kids played football, Cacá was dissecting telemetry data with his dad, learning the nuances of racing lines and throttle control. His professional career ignited in Stock Car Brasil, quickly establishing himself as a force to be reckoned with. A defining moment came at Interlagos in 2010, when, despite starting from the back of the grid due to a technical infringement, he carved his way through the field to snatch a dramatic victory on the last lap. Now in his peak years, he continues to compete at the highest level of Stock Car Brasil, driving for KTF Racing, constantly honing his skills and seeking that elusive championship title.
drivingStyle: Cacá is a master of precision and tire management. He doesn't often set the fastest lap in qualifying, but he's known for his consistent pace throughout a race distance. His approach to corners is calculated, prioritizing exit speed and minimizing wheelspin. In high-pressure situations, he remains remarkably calm, a trait honed from years of experience. He is known to be extremely kind to his equipment, ensuring the car is in good condition until the very end of the race.

careerHighlight: Winning the Stock Car Brasil championship in 2006, a culmination of years of dedication and unwavering focus.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the final race of the 2012 season, handing the championship to his rival.
